name: org.machanism.machai:machai-mcp-server
description: Machai MCP Server is a Java 17 Model Context Protocol server built on the Machai AI framework. It bridges MCP-compatible clients with Machai functional tools and prompts supplied by additional runtime libraries. The artifact focuses on server orchestration rather than bundled domain tools: it discovers Machai tool implementations on the classpath, adapts their metadata and parameters into MCP schemas, exposes prompts and resources where supported, routes requests to tool functions, and supports project-directory context for automation workflows. It can run locally over STDIO for desktop clients or remotely over HTTP using either stateless request handling or streamable session-oriented communication. The command-line application supports server name, version, project directory, port, and session mode options. It is useful for AI assistant integrations, developer automation, internal platform tooling, coding assistants, MCP gateways, custom GenAI tool publication, and deployments that need a reusable Java MCP server for independently packaged functional tool extensions.

usageContext: Run as a CLI application to expose Machai functional tools through MCP
Use STDIO mode for local MCP desktop clients
Use HTTP stateless mode for remote MCP clients
Use HTTP streamable session mode for clients requiring session-aware communication
Add additional Machai-compatible functional tool jars on the runtime classpath
Provide a project directory so tools can operate against a known workspace

constructors.description: Creates an HTTP stateless MCP server that reports the supplied server name and version to MCP clients. The server loads Machai GenAI tools through runtime configuration and exposes MCP APIs over Jetty when started with a configured port.

examples.description: Programmatically creates and starts a stateless HTTP MCP server on port 45000. Add Machai-compatible functional tool jars to the application classpath before running so the server can publish those tools.

constructors.description: Creates an HTTP streamable MCP server for session-aware MCP communication. It is appropriate when an HTTP client needs streamable transport behavior in addition to tool and prompt exposure.

examples.description: Programmatically creates a streamable HTTP MCP server. This mirrors CLI usage with the --port and --session options.

constructors.description: Creates an MCP server that communicates through standard input and output. STDIO mode is the default application mode when no port is supplied and is commonly used by local desktop MCP clients.

examples.description: Programmatically creates a STDIO MCP server for local client integrations. In normal deployments, prefer invoking org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer from the command line.

features.name: main
features.signature: public static void main(java.lang.String[] args) throws java.lang.Exception
features.description: Command-line entry point for the MCP server application. It parses options for help, project directory, server name, server version, HTTP port, and streamable session mode. Without a port, it starts a STDIO MCP server. With a port, it starts an HTTP MCP server; with both port and session, it starts streamable HTTP mode.

examples.description: Installs the component by placing the server jar and a functional tool container jar on the Java classpath, configures it with project directory, server metadata, HTTP port, and streamable session mode, then runs it as a remote MCP server.

features.name: tools
features.description: Loads and registers Machai GenAI tools with the selected MCP server. Tool implementations are supplied by additional libraries on the runtime classpath and are adapted into MCP-compatible tool specifications.

examples.description: Registers tools using a configuration file before starting the server. The practical deployment requirement is to include the server jar plus one or more Machai functional tool jars on the classpath.

features.name: start
features.description: Starts an MCP server transport. HTTP implementations initialize Jetty, configure thread pools and connectors, and register the MCP servlet transport provider. STDIO implementations expose MCP communication over process input and output.

examples.description: Starts a configured HTTP MCP server. For real-world use, register tools before start and ensure port 45000 is available.

features.name: addTool
features.signature: protected void addTool(java.lang.String name, java.lang.String description, org.machanism.machai.ai.tools.ToolFunction function, org.machanism.machai.ai.tools.ParamDescriptor... paramsDesc)
features.description: Converts a Machai tool function and parameter descriptors into an MCP tool schema and synchronous tool specification. This is the adapter mechanism used when publishing custom functional tools through the server.

examples.snippet:
// Implement custom tools in a separate Machai functional tool library, package the jar, then run:
java -cp /path/to/machai-mcp-server.jar:/path/to/custom-tools.jar org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer --port 45000
examples.description: Practical usage scenario for tool publication: create a custom functional tool jar, put it beside the MCP server on the classpath, and run the server so clients can discover and call the tool through MCP.

features.name: buildSpecification
features.description: Builds MCP synchronous tool specifications from generic tool definitions for STDIO or streamable HTTP server modes. Stateless HTTP mode has an equivalent builder for io.modelcontextprotocol.common.McpTransportContext.

examples.description: Creates the streamable HTTP tool specification builder used internally by the server adapter. Most users do not instantiate it directly; they run the CLI and let the server wire adapters automatically.

customizations.name: Functional tool libraries on the runtime classpath
customizations.description: The server intentionally does not bundle domain-specific tools. Deployments customize behavior by packaging Machai-compatible functional tool and prompt implementations in separate jars and adding them to the Java classpath when launching the server.

examples.description: Adds a team-specific tool library to the server deployment and exposes its capabilities through HTTP MCP.

customizations.name: Command-line options
customizations.description: Runtime behavior is configured with -h/--help, -d/--projectDir, -n/--name, -v/--version, -p/--port, and -s/--session. These options control transport selection, server metadata, project context, and streamable HTTP mode.

examples.description: Configures a stateless HTTP MCP server with explicit project directory and server metadata.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.AbstractMcpServer
studs.description: Base implementation for MCP servers. It defines common hooks for tool registration and server startup and manages project-directory context used by tools.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.AbstractMcpServer.ToolSpecificationBuilder
studs.description: Gateway contract for building transport-specific MCP tool specification objects from generic tool definitions and call handlers.

examples.title: Run in STDIO mode for a desktop MCP client
steps: Download machai-mcp-server.jar from the release page or build it with Maven.
Prepare at least one Machai-compatible functional tool jar and place it on the classpath.
Configure any required environment variables such as gw_model, embedding_model, GENAI_USERNAME, and GENAI_PASSWORD.
Configure the MCP client command to invoke the same Java command.
examples.description: STDIO mode is the default because no --port option is provided. It is appropriate for local clients such as Claude Desktop that launch the server as a child process.

examples.title: Run in HTTP mode and connect an MCP client
steps: Download or build machai-mcp-server.jar and collect the functional tool jars to publish.
Start the server with java -cp /path/to/machai-mcp-server.jar:/path/to/functional-tool-container.jar org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer --port 45000.
Configure a client to connect to http://localhost:45000/mcp, for example using mcp-remote or MCP Inspector.
Invoke tools from the client and check server logs if a tool requires missing credentials or configuration.
examples.description: HTTP mode makes the MCP server available to remote or separately launched clients. Add --session when a streamable session-aware HTTP transport is required.

examples.title: Build from source and create a packaged jar with dependencies
steps: Run mvn clean package to build the Maven project.
Run mvn -Ppack install to create the packaged distribution jar with dependencies.
Run the generated jar together with functional tool jars on the classpath.
examples.description: The Maven build uses Java 17 and includes an assembly profile that sets org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer as the main class for packaged releases.
